dialogue.question: What is a fever?
dialogue.answer: A fever is defined as a body temperature of 38 degrees Celsius or higher in adults.

retrieval.title: High temperature in adults
retrieval.text: In adults, a temperature of 38 degrees Celsius or higher is generally described as a fever. Body temperature varies between people and over the day. Feeling hot or shivery can matter even when a reading is lower.

dialogue.question: What causes a cough?
dialogue.answer: A cough can occur with various conditions including colds, flu, allergies, reflux, and other respiratory issues. It is important to consult a healthcare professional if the cough persists for more than three weeks.

retrieval.title: Cough and possible causes
retrieval.text: A cough can occur with a cold or flu, allergies, reflux or other conditions. A cough alone does not establish a diagnosis. NHS guidance recommends medical review for a persistent cough lasting more than three weeks.

retrieval.title: Shortness of breath
retrieval.text: Breathlessness has many possible causes. Treatment depends on the cause, so symptoms should not be used to self-diagnose. Severe breathing difficulty, such as gasping or being unable to get words out, requires immediate medical help.

dialogue.question: How can I correct evidence?
dialogue.answer: Users can correct evidence by changing a symptom's status in the evidence panel to Present, Absent, or Not sure. Corrections update the current evidence but retain historical data for recalculating candidate results.

retrieval.title: Unknown answers and uncertainty
retrieval.text: Not sure means that the symptom has not been confirmed or denied. It is stored separately and is not passed to recall as negative evidence. A user may correct this status later using the evidence panel.

retrieval.title: Correcting a symptom
retrieval.text: The evidence panel lets the user change a symptom to Present, Absent or Not sure. Corrections replace current evidence while retaining history. The application then recalculates candidate results using the updated evidence.
